purpose: Defines the obligations of readers who rely on ADRs when deciding to drop a proposal or review finding: ADRs are non-binding, rejection premises must be rechecked, and ADR numbers must be cited.
summary: ADRs are insights, not instructions; a proposal may still be made if the rejection reason is judged wrong
Reader obligation: verify the premises of the rejection reason still hold before relying on an ADR
Reader obligation: cite the ADR number and section (ADR-NNN §N) when dropping a proposal or finding
No mechanism is introduced to raise ADR reach, such as preloading all ADRs, because the loss is only a duplicate proposal
Severity catalog: omitting the ADR number when dropping a proposal is minor
Points to the ADR principles spec and ADR format for authors of ADRs
tasks: Making a proposal while checking past ADR decisions
Dropping a proposal based on an ADR rejection reason
Code or document review where a finding is dropped because of an ADR
Assigning severity to ADR usage violations
title: ADR 利用規範
